lines.text: Welcome to the final video.
Now you know what you're building.
You understand the building blocks.
You understand the code.
Now let's see how AI can help us build faster.
You could ask Claude, make me a dino game.
And you'd get a game. But it's not your game. It's not your design. You don't understand it. And when it breaks, you're stuck.
Here's how a creator asks. Five parts.
What I'm building. What I already have. What I understand. What I want. And what I need back.
Look at the last one. Explain the logic first. You're not asking AI to think for you. You're asking it to think with you.
Use one. Understanding.
Copy a function you don't fully get, and ask Claude to explain it in simple language.
Use AI like a patient tutor. Then ask a follow up. What happens if I make the padding bigger?
And then, test it. Don't just believe it. See it.
Use two. Debugging.
Imagine you accidentally deleted the landing check. The dinosaur falls through the floor.
Describe what you expected, what actually happened, and paste the code.
And ask why, before you ask for the fix.
If you only take the fix, you'll make the same mistake next week. If you understand why, you won't.
And you already knew this one. That's how you can tell when AI is right, and when it isn't.
Use three. Adding a feature.
We want the game to speed up every hundred points.
Logic first. Before any code, we check the idea in a table.
Then the code is short, and every line matches the logic.
Play to a hundred... and it speeds up.
Then question it. Will this get impossibly fast? Claude suggests a maximum speed. You're the one deciding.
Use four. Ideas.
Ask for three ways to make the game more interesting, without changing the core gameplay.
AI is great for ideas. But you choose. Which one fits your paper plan?
Let's add a best score. The idea goes back onto paper first. Even with AI, the process doesn't change.
Use five. Design.
Ask what you'd need to change for a jungle theme.
Claude points to our colour variables.
One block of colours, and the whole world changes. That's why we made variables in video three.
And notice. No JavaScript changes. Appearance and behaviour are separate jobs.
Five ways to use AI.
And every time, the same five steps.
Read it. Understand it. Test it. Question it. Improve it.
Look how far you've come.
Idea. Paper plan. HTML. CSS. JavaScript. A working game. AI. And an improved game.
You didn't just make a game.
You learned a process.
You started with an idea.
You imagined the finished product.
You put it on paper.
You broke it into pieces.
You built those pieces.
You tested them.
You solved problems.
And then you used AI to help you go further.
That process can be used to build far more than games.
It can help you build websites, apps, tools, businesses, creative projects, and ideas that don't exist yet.
You imagine it. You plan it. You build it.
